title: Advanced Practice Physiotherapy – A qualitative interview study on perspectives of relevant stakeholders in Germany
summary: The German healthcare system faces many challenges. In addition to an aging population and increasingly complex disease trajectories, there are growing shortages in care provision and a lack of skilled professionals. The care model “Advanced Practice Physiotherapy” (APP) can reduce waiting times, ease the burden on physicians, and lead to long-term cost savings. Advanced practice in physical therapy encompasses advanced knowledge, strong clinical reasoning skills, and sound clinical judgment. This enables specifically trained physiotherapists to manage and treat complex cases while taking risks into account. This requires knowledge and experience that go beyond a basic physical therapy education. In other countries, such as Canada or the UK, advanced practice physiotherapy has already been implemented or is an integral part of the healthcare system. Germany, however, is still in the early stages. Therefore, the aim of this study is to explore various perspectives on the potential for Advanced Practice Physiotherapy in Germany. Experts will be interviewed to identify potential, opportunities and risks. The survey will consist of 10–15 individual interviews, which will then be analyzed scientifically.
conditions: Potential for APP in the German healthcare system from the perspective of relevant stakeholders

interventions.name: Experts for APP in the German healthcare system will be interviewed using a semistructured interview format.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Working in one of the following stakeholder groups: researchers in the fields of therapeutic sciences, health services research, health economics, and related disciplines; interprofessional healthcare associations; physical therapy associations; physical therapists; academic institutions offering physical therapy programs
- Involvement (past or present) with professional development and/or innovative care models in physical therapy
- Working in Germany (currently or in the past)
- Individuals aged 18 or older who are capable of giving informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of knowledge about the German healthcare system
- Underaged
- Non-German-speaking
